highlights: Autonomous mobile UV-C system is positioned for pharmaceutical manufacturing environments
Robot movement addresses distance and shadowing limitations of fixed UV sources
Pharma software includes operator authentication and an audit trail

The Pharma FAQ gives an example of a 25 m² room in approximately ten minutes or less, depending on layout, size and target microorganism. This is a conditional room-cycle example, not battery endurance or a guaranteed hourly rate.

Pharma software is described by the manufacturer as supporting 21 CFR Part 11 through operator authentication, audit trails and data logging. The eight-document validation package includes site requirements, installation/operational qualification, room-specific cycle development and requalification; installation approval is not automatic.

Pharma features include laser scanners, 3D cameras, optional tablet-controlled manual navigation and fleet UV exposure maps with PDF export. The separately offered CARE+ programme supports ongoing service and reporting.

The FAQ distinguishes Log 3 targets for vegetative microorganisms from Log 2 for spores using UV-C alone; higher targets require longer exposure. These conditional targets do not establish a universal six-log reduction or clinical infection outcome.
